_meta.disclaimer: This library is for building a technology demo/MVP. It is not medical advice and should be reviewed by a licensed physiotherapist before clinical use with real patients.

abduction_deg.notes: 90° pure glenohumeral joint range; 150-180° with full shoulder girdle involvement. Source: Physiopedia Goniometry: Shoulder Abduction.

exercises.name: Shoulder Abduction
exercises.description: Patient stands with arms at sides, then raises both arms out to the side (away from the body) in the frontal plane up to shoulder height or as prescribed, then lowers with control.
common_compensations: Torso lateral lean toward the moving arm
Asymmetry between left and right arm angle
cues: Keep torso upright and centered
Raise arm slowly and with control, no swinging
Stop at shoulder height unless cleared for full overhead range

exercises.name: Shoulder Flexion (Wand/Active-Assisted)
exercises.description: Patient raises arm forward and upward in the sagittal plane, optionally assisted with a wand/stick held in both hands for early-stage rehab.
common_compensations: Lumbar arching to gain extra height
Elbow bending to shorten the lever
cues: Keep elbow straight
Avoid arching the lower back
Move within pain-free range only

exercises.name: Shoulder External Rotation
exercises.description: Elbow tucked at side and bent 90°, patient rotates forearm outward away from the body, typically with light resistance band.
cues: Keep elbow pinned to your side
Rotate only the forearm, not the whole arm

exercises.name: Shoulder Internal Rotation
exercises.description: Elbow tucked at side and bent 90°, patient rotates forearm inward across the body, typically with light resistance band.
common_compensations: Trunk rotation substituting for shoulder rotation
cues: Keep hips and torso facing forward
Elbow stays fixed at your side

exercises.name: Pendulum Swing
exercises.description: Patient bends forward slightly, supporting themselves on a table with the unaffected arm, and lets the affected arm hang and gently swing in small circles.
common_compensations: Using shoulder muscles to actively swing rather than allowing gravity/momentum
cues: Let the arm hang loose
Small, controlled circles, both directions
exercises.notes: Typically an early-stage, low-load mobility exercise (e.g. post-op, frozen shoulder, acute pain).

flexion_deg.notes: Functional minimums per Dietz et al., cited via Physiopedia Goniometry: Knee Flexion.

exercises.name: Quadriceps Set (Isometric)
exercises.description: Patient sits or lies with knee fully extended, and isometrically contracts the quadriceps (tightening the thigh muscle, pressing knee down) without moving the joint.
cues: Push the back of your knee down
Hold, then fully relax between reps

exercises.name: Straight Leg Raise
exercises.description: Patient lies supine, one knee bent for stability, the other leg kept straight with quadriceps engaged and lifted to roughly 45° of hip flexion, then lowered slowly.
cues: Lock the knee straight before lifting
Lower slowly over ~2 seconds, don't let it drop

exercises.name: Knee Flexion (Heel Slide)
exercises.description: Patient supine or seated, slides the heel toward the buttock to actively bend the knee through available range, then slides back out.
common_compensations: Hip hiking to compensate for restricted knee flexion
cues: Slide slowly and evenly
Stop at the point of tightness, not sharp pain

exercises.name: Mini Squat / Wall Sit
exercises.description: Patient performs a partial squat (or a wall sit hold) with knees tracking over toes, typically limited to 30-45° of knee flexion in early rehab.
cues: Keep knees pointed over your toes
Weight evenly on both feet
Don't let knees pass your toes

exercises.name: Standing Single-Leg Balance
exercises.description: Patient balances on the involved leg with a slight knee bend, maintaining hip-knee-foot alignment.
cues: Soft bend in the knee, not locked straight
Keep hips level

exercises.name: Step-Up
exercises.description: Patient steps up onto a low step leading with the involved leg, contracting quadriceps and hip muscles to bring both feet onto the step, then steps back down with control.
common_compensations: Pushing off with the trailing leg instead of the working leg
cues: Control the step down, don't just drop
Knee stays aligned over the foot

fifa_11_plus.purpose: Complete warm-up programme to reduce injuries in football players aged 14+; validated to reduce overall injury risk by ~30% and severe/ACL injury risk by up to ~50%.
fifa_11_plus.frequency: At least twice per week as standard warm-up before training; running-only version (Parts 1 and 3) before matches.

structure.name: Running Exercises
structure.focus: Slow-speed running combined with active stretching and controlled partner contacts; cutting, deceleration, landing technique.

structure.name: Strength, Plyometrics and Balance Exercises
structure.focus: Six exercise sets, each with 3 levels of increasing difficulty. Core strength, eccentric control, proprioception.

structure.name: Running Exercises
structure.focus: Moderate/high-speed running combined with planting and cutting movements.

key_technique_points: Straight leg alignment (hip-knee-foot in one line)
Knee-over-toe position, knees must not buckle inward (valgus) — this is the #1 form fault to detect visually
Soft, cushioned landings on the balls of the feet
Level 1 must be mastered before progressing to Level 2, then Level 3 (individually, per exercise, typically after 3-4 weeks)

part1_running_exercises.name: Straight Ahead
part1_running_exercises.description: Jog straight to the last cone; run slightly faster on the way back. Twice.
part1_running_exercises.cue: Upper body straight; hips/knees/feet aligned; knees must not buckle inward.

part1_running_exercises.name: Hip Out
part1_running_exercises.description: Jog to a cone, lift knee forward, rotate knee out to the side, place foot down; repeat other leg. Twice.
part1_running_exercises.cue: Pelvis horizontal, core still; supporting-leg knee must not buckle inward.

part1_running_exercises.name: Hip In
part1_running_exercises.description: Jog to a cone, lift knee to the side, rotate knee forward, place foot down; repeat other leg. Twice.
part1_running_exercises.cue: Pelvis horizontal, core still; supporting-leg knee must not buckle inward.

part1_running_exercises.name: Circling Partner
part1_running_exercises.description: Jog forward, shuffle sideways to partner, circle around each other, shuffle/jog back. Twice.
part1_running_exercises.cue: Slight hip/knee bend, weight on balls of feet; knees must not buckle inward.

part1_running_exercises.name: Jumping with Shoulder Contact
part1_running_exercises.description: Jog and shuffle toward partner, jump sideways to make shoulder-to-shoulder contact, shuffle back. Twice.
part1_running_exercises.cue: Land on both feet with hips/knees bent; knees must not buckle inward.

part1_running_exercises.name: Quick Forwards and Backwards Sprints
part1_running_exercises.description: Sprint forward two cones, sprint backward one cone, repeat; hips/knees slightly bent throughout.
part1_running_exercises.cue: Upper body straight, hips/knees/feet aligned; knees must not buckle inward.

part2_strength_plyo_balance_exercises.name: The Bench (Plank)

levels.name: Static
levels.description: Front plank on forearms and feet, straight line head-to-foot, hold.

levels.name: Alternate Legs
levels.description: Same plank position, lift each leg in turn for a 2-second count.

levels.name: One Leg Lift and Hold
levels.description: Same plank position, lift one leg 10-15cm and hold, then switch sides.

cues: Straight line head to feet
Elbows directly under shoulders
Do not let hips sag or buttocks rise
Keep pelvis level, don't let it tilt

part2_strength_plyo_balance_exercises.name: Sideways Bench (Side Plank)

levels.name: Static
levels.description: Side plank, lowermost knee bent 90°, hold.

levels.name: Raise and Lower Hip
levels.description: Side plank with legs straight, raise/lower hips repeatedly.

levels.name: With Leg Lift
levels.description: Side plank with legs straight, lift and lower the top leg.

cues: Shoulder-hip-leg in one straight line
Elbow directly under shoulder
Pelvis must not tilt down or forward/back

part2_strength_plyo_balance_exercises.name: Hamstrings (Nordic Curl style, partner-assisted)
part2_strength_plyo_balance_exercises.description: Kneeling, partner holds ankles down, patient leans forward slowly resisting with hamstrings, catching self with hands when control is lost.
cues: Head-body-hips-thighs in a straight line
Movement only at the knee joint
Do not bend at the hips

part2_strength_plyo_balance_exercises.name: Single-Leg Stance (Balance)

levels.name: Hold the Ball
levels.description: Balance on one leg holding a ball in both hands.

levels.name: Throwing Ball with Partner
levels.description: Balance on one leg while throwing a ball with a partner.

levels.name: Test Your Partner
levels.description: Balance on one leg while partner tries to push you off balance.

cues: Hip-knee-foot in a straight line
Supporting knee slightly bent, not locked
Weight on the ball of the foot
Knee must not buckle inward, pelvis must not tilt

part2_strength_plyo_balance_exercises.name: Squats

levels.name: With Toe Raise
levels.description: Squat to ~90° knee flexion leaning torso forward, straighten up, rise onto toes, lower.

levels.name: Walking Lunges
levels.description: Forward lunges, front knee flexed to 90°, front knee must not pass the toes.

levels.name: One-Leg Squats
levels.description: Single-leg squat with a partner for light support, bend knee toward 90°, straighten.

cues: Hip-knee-foot in two straight parallel lines
Knee must not buckle inward
Bent knee should not extend beyond the toes
Keep pelvis horizontal

part2_strength_plyo_balance_exercises.name: Jumping

levels.name: Vertical Jumps
levels.description: Squat to 90°, hold 1 sec, jump as high as possible, land soft on balls of feet.

levels.name: Lateral Jumps
levels.description: Single-leg lateral jumps ~1m side to side, landing soft each time.

levels.name: Box Jumps (Cross Pattern)
levels.description: Jump forward/backward/side-to-side/diagonal around a center point as quickly as possible.

cues: Land on the balls of the feet with soft, bent knees
Cushioned landing and powerful take-off matter more than jump height
Knees must never meet or buckle inward
Do not land with locked knees or on the heels

part3_running_exercises.name: Across the Pitch
part3_running_exercises.description: Run ~40m at 75-80% max pace, jog the remainder, jog back. Twice.
part3_running_exercises.cue: Upper body straight; knees must not buckle inward.

part3_running_exercises.name: Bounding
part3_running_exercises.description: 6-8 bounding steps with high knee lift, opposite arm swinging across the body, jog to recover. Twice.
part3_running_exercises.cue: Upper body straight; land on the ball of the leading foot; knee must not buckle inward.

part3_running_exercises.name: Plant and Cut
part3_running_exercises.description: Jog 4-5 steps, plant and cut direction, sprint 5-7 steps at 80-90% max pace, repeat alternating sides. Twice.
part3_running_exercises.cue: Upper body straight, hips/knees/feet aligned; knees must not buckle inward.

sports_screening.purpose: Quick movement-quality screen to flag common injury-risk patterns before activity, using the same pose-estimation engine as clinical rehab.

measured_signals.description: Knees track inward past the line of the toes/ankles during descent.
Torso leans forward beyond a threshold angle, often indicating limited ankle/hip mobility or weak posterior chain.
One side descends further or bears more visible weight than the other.
Heels lift off the ground during the squat.
risk_flagged_for: Limited ankle dorsiflexion, compensatory knee/hip loading

risk_flag_recommendations.recommendation: Consider hip abductor and gluteal strengthening (e.g. FIFA 11+ single-leg stance and squat exercises).
Consider ankle mobility work and core/posterior chain strengthening (e.g. FIFA 11+ Bench/Sideways Bench series).
Consider unilateral strength assessment and single-leg balance training (FIFA 11+ Single-Leg Stance series).
Consider calf and ankle mobility exercises before progressing to jump/plyometric work.

sports_screening.note: Thresholds (e.g. exact valgus angle, exact lean angle) should be tuned against pilot video data; the FIFA 11+ manual explicitly identifies knee-over-toe alignment and straight leg alignment as the core visual form check across nearly all of its exercises, which maps directly onto this screening logic.
